title: Six Dead, Including Two Children, After Small Plane Crashes Off Mississippi Coast
snippet: A tragic plane crash off the Mississippi Gulf Coast has claimed the lives of six people, including an 8-year-old and a 10-year-old boy, as federal authorities launch an investigation.
content:
A devastating aviation tragedy unfolded off the Mississippi Gulf Coast on Tuesday afternoon when a small private aircraft crashed into the ocean, killing all six people on board, including two young children.

According to the U.S. Coast Guard, the single-engine Cessna 210 was en route from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida, when air traffic controllers suddenly lost contact with the aircraft at around 3:45 p.m. Flight data revealed that the plane plummeted in a rapid, steep descent of roughly 10,000 feet per minute before crashing into the Gulf waters about two miles northeast of Horn Island, near Pascagoula.

Search and Recovery Operation

Following an intensive four-hour multi-agency search effort, Coast Guard divers located the wreckage of the submerged plane. Officials confirmed early Wednesday that the remains of all six victims—four adults and two young boys, aged 8 and 10—were recovered from inside the fuselage.

"This is a heartbreaking outcome, and our deepest sympathies are with the families and loved ones who are facing an unimaginable loss," said Cmdr. Trevor Blount, search and rescue mission coordinator for Coast Guard Sector Mobile. Blount commended the close interagency response that enabled search teams to locate the aircraft quickly and provide closure to the families involved.

Federal Probe Launched

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) have initiated a joint investigation to determine the root cause of the sudden plunge. The identities of the victims have been withheld pending complete notification of next of kin.
